findings.title: Early return when date override exists skips busy time checks
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, if a date override exists for the slot's date and the slot falls within the override's bounds, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately `return true` before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. As a result, any existing bookings or calendar busy times on a day with a date override are completely ignored, allowing double-bookings during overridden hours.

findings.title: Dayjs object reference comparison with `===` is always false and boundary checks are wrong
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 114 compares two newly constructed Dayjs instances using `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and always evaluates to `false` instead of detecting an all-day unavailable override (where start equals end). Furthermore, the range checks on lines 118-125 use `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` and `slotStartTime > overrideEnd` instead of checking whether the entire slot `[slotStartTime, slotEndTime]` fits within `[overrideStart, overrideEnd]` (i.e. `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`), allowing slots that only partially overlap the override window.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day or across UTC midnight are not handled
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` rejects the slot as soon as the first override on that date does not contain the slot. If a user configures multiple date override time ranges on the same day (split shifts), any slot in the second range will fail against the first range and be marked unavailable. Additionally, `dateOverrides` from `getUserAvailability` are already converted to UTC timestamps, so adding `utcOffset` again shifts the override time a second time and comparing `format("YYYY MM DD")` in UTC fails when the override crosses UTC midnight.

findings.title: Working hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and fails on split working hours
findings.body: In the `workingHours.find` block (lines 139-147), `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after working hours is not rejected. Also, because `.find()` returns truthy if *any* working-hour entry for that day does not contain the slot, a user with multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g., 9:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) will have all slots rejected because every slot lies outside at least one of the blocks.

findings.title: Double timezone offset applied to `dateOverrides` in `getSlots`
findings.body: `getUserAvailability` already shifts `dateOverrides` start and end dates from the organizer's timezone into UTC. In `getSlots`, lines 212-223 compute `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and add it to `dayjs(override.start).utc()`. Because `override.start` is already in UTC (not in local organizer time stored as UTC), subtracting `organizerUtcOffset` again shifts the override by the organizer's offset a second time. Furthermore, `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` wraps around modulo 1440 if adding the offset crosses midnight in the invitee's timezone.
